Title: OpenChatCut Review: A Free Open-Source AI Video Editor With an Editable Timeline - Abdul Aziz Ahwan
# OpenChatCut Review: A Free Open-Source AI Video Editor With an Editable Timeline. AI video tools can generate clips quickly, but many of them leave creators with a frustrating limitation: the final result is difficult to edit. OpenChatCut approaches the problem differently by combining conversational AI with a real, professional-style video-editing timeline. Instead of asking an AI to produce a flattened video, you can describe the edit you want and let an agent organize clips, trim pauses, add captions, place music, build transitions, and adjust the project timeline. **OpenChatCut** is also free, open source, and designed around a local-first workflow, making it an interesting option for creators, developers, marketers, educators, and anyone searching for an open-source ChatCut alternative. Download OpenChatCut, import your footage, and tell the AI agent how you want the video edited. ## What Is OpenChatCut? OpenChatCut is an open-source, agent-native video editor that brings natural-language instructions and conventional timeline editing into the same workspace. It is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with the commercial ChatCut product. The editor gives AI agents access to actual editing tools. When you request a faster introduction, automatic captions, a different soundtrack, or a transition between two clips, the agent can apply those changes directly to the project. You can then preview the result, manually refine individual tracks, undo unwanted actions, or continue the conversation with another instruction. This creates a workflow that sits between a traditional non-linear editor and a one-shot AI video generator:. * The result is written to real tracks and clips. The agent reads the project context, including imported media, the current selection, transcript information, tracks, and timeline state. OpenChatCut includes a real multitrack editing environment for video, audio, captions, effects, and motion graphics. The application exposes a local MCP endpoint that allows compatible external agents to inspect and modify a video project. 3. **Let the agent inspect the project:** The agent reads the available media, transcript, timeline, tracks, and current selection. The combination of a local-first architecture, editable multitrack timeline, transcript tools, media generation, motion graphics, and MCP support makes it one of the more technically interesting open-source AI video editors available.

## Things that were harder than expected

 Caption sync. Whisper word timestamps are good but not perfect; landing captions on the right frame after silence-removal cuts meant treating the transcript timeline as the single source of truth and deriving the video from it, never the other way around.
 Multi-provider JSON. OpenAI's json\_object response format is silently ignored by some providers and errors on others. The fix: only send it where it's supported, and tolerantly parse fenced/prose-wrapped JSON everywhere else.
 No libass on some ffmpeg builds, so captions are rendered with Pillow and overlaid instead of relying on the subtitle filter.

## Try it

It's a docker compose up away, or run it with uv / pip. You only add one LLM key.

 Repo: 
 Site: [...] 2. The "brain" — an LLM (your key). This is the only thing that touches the network. The model does two jobs: scoring the strongest moments in the transcript (hook / flow / value, not a keyword scan), and turning a plain-language request like "make it punchier" into a sequence of concrete edit actions.

3. Rendering — ffmpeg (local). Every cut, 9:16 reframe, caption burn, zoom and audio duck is an ffmpeg operation. No cloud render farm.

The chat layer is a tool-calling agent. When you type "cut the silences" the model never touches the video — it calls a tool that operates on the transcript timestamps, and the actual pixels are produced by replaying cached intermediates through ffmpeg. One undo reverts a whole multi-step plan, because every mutation is a snapshot. [...] Skip to content

# How I built an open-source AI video editor you control by chatting

#python #ai #ffmpeg #opensource

A few months ago I had a folder full of long videos — podcast recordings, talks, screen recordings — and one simple goal: turn them into short vertical clips with captions. Every tool I tried wanted me to either drag clips around a timeline for an hour, or upload my raw footage to someone's cloud and pay per export.

So I built my own, and I just open-sourced it. It's called VibeClip, and the core idea is simple: you edit by typing what you want.
